solution.en: The outer loop runs J from 5 down to 1 (STEP -1). For each value of J, the inner loop runs I from 1 to J, printing each I with a trailing semicolon (so the numbers appear on the same line, separated by spaces). After the inner loop finishes, a plain 'PRINT' statement (with no value) moves output to a new line before the next value of J. This produces a decreasing right-angled triangle of numbers: J=5 prints 1 2 3 4 5; J=4 prints 1 2 3 4; J=3 prints 1 2 3; J=2 prints 1 2; J=1 prints 1.
solution.ne: The outer loop runs J from 5 down to 1 (STEP -1). For each value of J, the inner loop runs I from 1 to J, printing each I with a trailing semicolon (so the numbers appear on the same line, separated by spaces). After the inner loop finishes, a plain 'PRINT' statement (with no value) moves output to a new line before the next value of J. This produces a decreasing right-angled triangle of numbers: J=5 prints 1 2 3 4 5; J=4 prints 1 2 3 4; J=3 prints 1 2 3; J=2 prints 1 2; J=1 prints 1.

items.code:
DECLARE SUB SERIES ()
CLS
CALL SERIES
END

SUB SERIES
FOR J = 5 TO 1 STEP -1
    FOR I = 1 TO J
        PRINT I;
    NEXT I
    PRINT
NEXT J
END SUB

title.ne: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program

answer.en: The program has three bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement referencing the wrong file number, and CLOSE not specifying which file to close.
answer.ne: The program has three bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement referencing the wrong file number, and CLOSE not specifying which file to close.

solution.en: (1) 'OPEN "REC.DAT" FOR OUTPUT AS #1' would erase any existing data; since the comment says more data should be added to an existing file, it must be 'FOR APPEND AS #1'. (2) 'INPUT #2, N$, A$, C$, RN' both reads from the file instead of writing to it, and refers to file #2 which was never opened (the file was opened as #1); to add a record it must be 'WRITE #1, N$, A$, C$, RN'. (3) 'CLOSE' with no file number closes all open files by default, which happens to work here since only one file is open, but it has been made explicit as 'CLOSE #1' to clearly match the file that was opened. Note: the filename has also been cleaned from the scanned 'REC. DAT' (with a stray space) to 'REC.DAT'; please verify this against the original paper.

solution.en: A is the Real (actual) parameter - the variable holding the value 1234 that is passed into the function when it is called as 'Y = SUM(A)'. N is the Formal parameter - the name used inside 'FUNCTION SUM(N)' to receive and refer to that passed-in value within the function body.
solution.ne: A is the Real (actual) parameter - the variable holding the value 1234 that is passed into the function when it is called as 'Y = SUM(A)'. N is the Formal parameter - the name used inside 'FUNCTION SUM(N)' to receive and refer to that passed-in value within the function body.

items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION SUM (N)
CLS
A = 1234
Y = SUM (A)
PRINT "Sum of individual digits"; Y
END

FUNCTION SUM (N)
    WHILE N<>0
        D = N MOD 10
        S = S+D
        N = INT (N/10)
    WEND
    SUM = S
END FUNCTION

answer.en: The loop will continue infinitely (it will never terminate).
answer.ne: The loop will continue infinitely (it will never terminate).

solution.en: The line 'N = INT(N/10)' is what removes the last digit from N on every pass, gradually reducing N toward 0 so that the condition 'WHILE N<>0' eventually becomes false. If this line is removed, N never changes and always stays equal to its original value (1234), so the condition N<>0 remains true forever, causing an infinite loop that never terminates.

answer.en: A QBASIC program using a user-defined Function for the Total Surface Area and a Sub procedure for the Perimeter, as shown in the code field.
answer.ne: A QBASIC program using a user-defined Function for the Total Surface Area and a Sub procedure for the Perimeter, as shown in the code field.

solution.en: The main module takes the room's length (L), breadth (B), and height (H) as input. It calls the user-defined Function TSA(L, B, H), which returns 2*(LB+BH+HL) as given in the hint, and prints the result directly since a function returns a value. It then calls the Sub procedure Perimeter(L, B) using CALL, which computes 2*(L+B) internally and prints it itself, since a sub does not return a value to the caller.
solution.ne: The main module takes the room's length (L), breadth (B), and height (H) as input. It calls the user-defined Function TSA(L, B, H), which returns 2*(LB+BH+HL) as given in the hint, and prints the result directly since a function returns a value. It then calls the Sub procedure Perimeter(L, B) using CALL, which computes 2*(L+B) internally and prints it itself, since a sub does not return a value to the caller.

items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION TSA (L, B, H)
DECLARE SUB Perimeter (L, B)

CLS
INPUT "Enter length of room: ", L
INPUT "Enter breadth of room: ", B
INPUT "Enter height of room: ", H

PRINT "Total Surface Area = "; TSA(L, B, H)
CALL Perimeter(L, B)

END

FUNCTION TSA (L, B, H)
    TSA = 2 * (L * B + B * H + H * L)
END FUNCTION

SUB Perimeter (L, B)
    P = 2 * (L + B)
    PRINT "Perimeter = "; P
END SUB

OPEN "mark.txt" FOR INPUT AS #1
CLS
PRINT "Students with GPA greater than 2.8:"

    INPUT #1, RollNo, Name$, GPA
    IF GPA > 2.8 THEN
        PRINT RollNo, Name$, GPA
    END IF
LOOP
CLOSE #1
